source.title: Some Open Problems Related to Fixed Point Properties

accepted.question_text: Let S be a semitopological semigroup. Consider the fixed point property (fpp*) saying that whenever S = {T_s : s in S} is represented by norm nonexpansive mappings on a nonempty weak* compact convex subset C of the dual E* of a Banach space E, and the action map (s, x) -> T_s(x) from S x C to C is jointly continuous when C carries the weak* topology, then C contains a common fixed point for S. If LUC(S), the space of left uniformly continuous bounded functions on S, has a left invariant mean, must S have property (fpp*)?

evidence.quote: (fpp∗) Whenever S = {Ts : s ∈ S} is a representation of S as norm nonex￾pansive mappings on a nonempty weak* compact convex set C of the dual space of a Banach space E and the mapping (s, x) 7→ Ts(x) from S × C to C is jointly continuous, where C is equipped with the weak* topology of E∗, then there is a common fixed point for S in C.
Problem 2.1. Does a semitopological semigroup S have the fixed point property (fpp∗) if LUC(S) has a LIM?

accepted.question_text: Suppose LUC(S) has a left invariant mean for a semitopological semigroup S. Is the linear span of all left invariant means on LUC(S), equivalently the fixed point set of the adjoint operators of left translations acting on the set of means, necessarily finite dimensional?
accepted.context_brief: Dimension of invariant means on LUC(S)

evidence.quote: Problem 2.2. Suppose that LUC(S) has a left invariant mean. Does the linear span of the set of left invariant means on LUC(S) (i.e. the fixed point set of the adjoint operators of left translations on the set of means) form a finite dimensional space?

accepted.question_text: Let A be an F-algebra. If A is left amenable, so that A has topological left invariant means on its dual M = A*, under what conditions is the vector space spanned by the set of topological left invariant means on A finite dimensional?

evidence.quote: The F-algebra A is left amenable if there is a topological left invariant mean (abbreviated TLIM) m on A∗ = M, i.e. if there is m ∈ M∗ such that kmk = 1 and hm, ϕ·fi = hm, fi for all f ∈ M and all ϕ ∈ A with kϕk = h1, ϕi = 1 ...
Problem 2.3. Suppose that the F-algebra A is left amenable. When is the space spanned by the set of topological left invariant means on A finite dimensional?

accepted.question_text: Let S be a discrete semigroup. Define (fpp*s) to mean that whenever S = {T_s : s in S} is a norm nonexpansive representation on a nonempty norm-separable weak* compact convex subset C of the dual E* of a Banach space E, and (s, x) -> T_s(x) from S x C to C is jointly continuous when C carries the weak* topology, then C has a common fixed point. If S has property (fpp*s), must WAP(S) have a left invariant mean? Conversely, if WAP(S) has a left invariant mean, is that sufficient to ensure (fpp*s)?

evidence.quote: (fpp∗s) Whenever S = {Ts : s ∈ S} is a norm nonexpansive representation of S on a nonempty norm separable weak* compact convex set C of the dual space of a Banach space E and the mapping (s, x) 7→ Ts(x) from S × C to C is jointly continuous when C is endowed with the weak* topology of E∗, then there is a common fixed point for S in C.

Problem 2.4. Let S be a (discrete) semigroup. If the fixed point property (fpp∗s) holds, does W AP(S) have a LIM? We also do not know whether the existence of a LIM on W AP(S) is sufficient to ensure the fixed point property (fpp∗s).

accepted.question_text: Let S_2 be the partially bicyclic semigroup generated by e, a, b, c with relation ab = e and ac = e. Does S_2 have the fixed point property (fpp*s), namely: every norm nonexpansive representation of S_2 on a nonempty norm-separable weak* compact convex subset of a dual Banach space, jointly continuous for the weak* topology, has a common fixed point?
accepted.context_brief: Partially bicyclic semigroup S2 and fpp*s

evidence.quote: Consider partially bicyclic semigroups S2 = he, a, b, c | ab = e, ac = ei and S1,1 = he, a, b, c, d | ab = e, cd = ei.

(fpp∗s) Whenever S = {Ts : s ∈ S} is a norm nonexpansive representation of S on a nonempty norm separable weak* compact convex set C of the dual space of a Banach space E and the mapping (s, x) 7→ Ts(x) from S × C to C is jointly continuous when C is endowed with the weak* topology of E∗, then there is a common fixed point for S in C.
Problem 2.6. Does the partially bicyclic semigroup S2 have the fixed point prop￾erty (fpp∗s)?

accepted.question_text: Let S be a semitopological semigroup such that WAP(S) has a left invariant mean. Must S satisfy the fixed point property (fppwq): whenever S acts on a weakly compact convex subset K of a separated locally convex space (E, Q) and the action is weakly separately continuous, weakly quasi-equicontinuous, and Q-nonexpansive, K contains a common fixed point for S?

evidence.quote: (fppwq) Whenever S acts on a weakly compact convex subset K of a separated locally convex space (E, Q) and the action is weakly separately continu￾ous, weakly quasi-equicontinuous and Q-nonexpansive, then K contains a common fixed point for S.
The converse is an open problem.
Problem 2.7. Does fpp (fppwq) hold for a semitopological semigroup S if W AP(S) has a LIM?

accepted.question_text: For a semitopological semigroup S, consider the fixed point properties (fppw), (fppwq), (fppwe), and (fppQ), where the paper states the implication chain fppw => fppwq => fppwe => fppQ. Can any of these implications be reversed?
accepted.context_brief: Reverse implications among fixed point properties

evidence.quote: (fppw) Whenever S acts on a weakly compact convex subset K of a separated locally convex space (E, Q) and the action is weakly separately continuous and Q-nonexpansive, then K contains a common fixed point for S.

(fppwq) Whenever S acts on a weakly compact convex subset K of a separated locally convex space (E, Q) and the action is weakly separately continu￾ous, weakly quasi-equicontinuous and Q-nonexpansive, then K contains a common fixed point for S.

(fppwe) Whenever S acts on a weakly compact convex subset K of a separated locally convex space (E, Q) and the action is weakly separately continuous, weakly equicontinuous and Q-nonexpansive, then K contains a common fixed point for S.
(fppQ) Whenever S acts on a compact convex subset K of a separated lo￾cally convex space (E, Q) and the action is separately continuous and Q￾nonexpansive, then K contains a common fixed point for S.
Clearly, we have the implication relations fppw ⇒ fppwq ⇒ fppwe ⇒ fppQ.
Problem 2.8. Can any of the above implications be reversed?

accepted.question_text: Let S be a left reversible semitopological semigroup acting by norm nonexpansive, weakly jointly continuous self-mappings on a nonempty weakly closed subset C of a Hilbert space. Assume there exists c in C such that the orbit {T_s c : s in S} is bounded. Must C contain a common fixed point for S? Equivalently, is the separability assumption removable from the known affirmative result for separable S?
accepted.context_brief: Left reversible semigroup actions on Hilbert spaces

evidence.quote: Problem 2.9. Let S be a left reversible semitopological semigroup acting on a weakly closed subset C 6= ∅ of a Hilbert space as norm nonexpansive and weakly jointly continuous self mappings. Suppose that there is c ∈ C such that {Tsc : s ∈ S} is bounded. Does C contain a common fixed point for S?
The question has been answered affirmatively in [16, Theorem 4.8] for the case that S is separable. We wonder whether the separability condition is removable.

accepted.question_text: A cited result states that a nonexpansive representation of a semitopological semigroup S on a nonempty closed convex subset C of a Hilbert space has a common fixed point in C whenever there exists c in C with bounded orbit {T_s c : s in S} and one of the following holds: (i) C_b(S) has a left invariant mean and s -> T_s c is continuous from S into (C, weak topology); (ii) S is left amenable and the action is weakly jointly continuous; (iii) AP(S) has a left invariant mean and the action is weakly separately continuous and weakly equicontinuous; or (iv) WAP(S) has a left invariant mean and the action is weakly separately continuous and weakly quasi-equicontinuous. In any of these four cases, does the converse hold?
accepted.context_brief: Converses to four Hilbert-space fixed point criteria

evidence.quote: It was also shown in [16, Theorem 4.3] that a nonexpansive representation of a semitopological semigroup S on a nonempty closed convex subset C of a Hilbert space H has a common fixed point in C if there is c ∈ C such that {Tsc : s ∈ S} is bounded and any of the following conditions holds:

(i) Cb(S) has a left invariant mean and the mapping s 7→ Tsc is continuous from S into (C, wk); (ii) S is left amenable and the action of S on C is weakly jointly continuous; (iii) AP(S) has a left invariant mean and the action of S on C is weakly sepa￾rately continuous and weakly equicontinuous continuous; (iv) W AP(S) has a left invariant mean and the action of S on C is weakly separately continuous and weakly quasi-equicontinuous.
Problem 2.10. In any of the cases in the above result, does the converse also hold?

accepted.question_text: Which amenability property of a semitopological semigroup is characterized by the Schauder fixed point property (fppS), namely: every jointly continuous representation of the semigroup on a nonempty compact convex subset of a separated locally convex topological vector space has a common fixed point?
accepted.context_brief: Amenability characterized by Schauder fixed point property

evidence.quote: (fppS ) Every jointly continuous representation of S on a nonempty compact convex subset C of a separated locally convex topological vector space has a common fixed point.
Problem 2.11. What amenability property of a semitopological semigroup may be characterized by the Schauder fixed point property (fppS )?

accepted.question_text: Let S be an extremely left amenable semitopological semigroup, and let C be a weakly closed subset of a Banach space E. Suppose S acts on C by a weakly continuous norm nonexpansive representation {T_s : s in S}, and for some c in C the orbit {T_s c : s in S} is relatively weakly compact. Must C contain a common fixed point for S?
accepted.context_brief: ELA semigroups and weak fixed points in Banach spaces

evidence.quote: We call a semitopological semigroup S extremely left amenable (abbreviated ELA) if there is a left invariant mean m on LUC(S) which is multiplicative ...

Problem 2.12. Suppose that S is extremely left amenable and C is a weakly closed subset of a Banach space E, and suppose that S = {Tsc : s ∈ S} is a weakly continuous and norm nonexpansive representation of S on C such that {Tsc : s ∈ S} is relatively weakly compact for some c ∈ C. Does C contain a common fixed point for S?

accepted.question_text: Let C be a nonempty closed convex subset of the sequence space c_0, and let S be a commutative semigroup acting on C by nonexpansive mappings {T_s : s in S}. If for some c in C the orbit {T_s c : s in S} is relatively weakly compact, must C contain a common fixed point for S?
accepted.context_brief: Commutative nonexpansive semigroup actions on c0

evidence.quote: Problem 2.13. Let C be a nonempty closed convex subset of the sequence space c0 and S = {Tsc : s ∈ S} be a representation of a commutative semigroup S as nonexpansive mappings on C. Suppose that {Tsc : s ∈ S} is relatively weakly compact for some c ∈ C. Does C contain a common fixed point for S?

accepted.question_text: Let A be an F-algebra. Property (F_n) says that for every separated locally convex vector space E and every linear representation of S = P_1(A) on E that is jointly continuous on compact subsets, if X is an n-consistent subset of E and there exists a closed S-invariant subspace H of codimension n such that (x + H) intersect X is compact for each x in E, then there exists an n-dimensional subspace L_0 contained in X with T_s(L_0) = L_0 for all s in S. Let (F' _n) be the same property with joint continuity on compact sets weakened to separate continuity on compact sets. Does (F_n) imply (F' _n)?

evidence.quote: (Fn) Let E be a separated locally convex vector space and S = {Tsc : s ∈ S} a linear representation of S = P1(A) on E such that the representation is jointly continuous on compact subsets of E . If X is a subset of E that is n-consistent with respect to S, and if there is a closed S-invariant subspace H of E with codimension n such that (x + H) ∩ X is compact for each x ∈ E, then there is L0 ∈ Ln(X) such that Ts(L0) = L0 (s ∈ S).
Let (F0n) denote the same property as (Fn) with “jointly continuous” replaced by “separately continuous” on compact subsets of E.
Problem 2.14. Let A be an F-algebra. Does (Fn) imply (F0n)?

accepted.question_text: Let A be an F-algebra. Let AP(A) denote the almost periodic functionals on A, and let (F^A_n) denote the same invariant-subspace property as (F_n) but with equicontinuity on compact subsets of E in place of joint continuity. If AP(A) has a topological left invariant mean, does A satisfy (F^A_n) for every integer n >= 1?

evidence.quote: Let (FA n ) denote the same property as (Fn) with joint continuity replaced by equicontinuity on compact subsets of E. It is known that if A satisfies (FA n ) then AP(A) has a TLIM (see [9]).
Problem 2.15. Does the existence of TLIM on AP(A) imply (FA n ) for all n ≥ 1?

accepted.question_text: Let A be an F-algebra. Let WAP(A) denote the weakly almost periodic functionals on A, and let (F^W_n) be the same invariant-subspace property as (F^A_n) except that equicontinuity on compact subsets is weakened to quasi-equicontinuity on compact subsets. If WAP(A) has a topological left invariant mean, does A satisfy (F^W_n) for every integer n >= 1?

evidence.quote: Let (F W n ) denote the same property (FA n ) with equicontinuity on compact subsets of E replaced by quasi-equicontinuity on compact subsets of E ... We have known that if A satisfies (F W n ) for each n ≥ 1 then W AP(A) has a TLIM (see [9]).
Problem 2.16. Does the existence of TLIM on W AP(A) imply (F W n ) for all n ≥ 1?

accepted.question_text: Let T be a norm nonexpansive self-map of a weak* compact subset K of a dual Banach space. Must T be pseudo weak*-nonexpansive, meaning that for each functional phi in the unit ball of the predual and each epsilon > 0 there exists a finite set Lambda in that unit ball such that |<phi, Tx - Ty>| <= max_{phi' in Lambda} |<phi', x - y>| + epsilon for all x, y in K?

evidence.quote: We call T pseudo weak*-nonexpansive if, for each φ ∈ E1 and each ε > 0, there exists a finite set Λ ⊂ E1 such that |hφ, T x − T yi| ≤ max φ0∈Λ |hφ0, x − yi| + ε for all x, y ∈ K.
Problem 2.17. Let T be a norm nonexpansive self mapping on a weak* compact subset of a dual Banach space. Must it be pseudo weak*-nonexpansive?

accepted.question_text: Let S be a semitopological semigroup such that AP(S) has a left invariant mean. Does S have the fixed point property (fpp*n): whenever K is a nonempty weak* compact convex subset of a dual Banach space with normal structure, every norm nonexpansive and separately weak* continuous representation of S on K has a common fixed point in K?

evidence.quote: (fpp∗n) If K is a nonempty weak* compact convex subset of a dual Banach space and if K has the normal structure, then a norm nonexpansive and separately weak* continuous representation of S on K has a common fixed point in K.
It is also known that if S is left reversible, then AP(S) has a LIM, and the converse is untrue [5].
Problem 2.18. Let S be a semitopological semigroup such that AP(S) has a LIM. Does the above fixed point property (fpp∗n) hold?
